excerpt: Use the first three months to turn an arrival address into a home that suits your routine. Plan temporary accommodation, neighbourhood research, documents and move-in costs in the right order.
introduction:
Your first address in the UAE does not have to answer every question about your future. It needs to make arrival manageable while you learn where work, school and everyday life will actually take place. A rushed long-term choice can be harder to undo than an imperfect temporary base.

Think of the first ninety days as a planning window, not a legal deadline or a visa allowance. The stages below are an adaptable household plan. Employment, residency, school admissions and tenancy requirements follow their own processes and may change the order or pace of your move.
takeaways: Choose an arrival base that supports the search, rather than judging it as your permanent home.
Confirm documents, payment timing and the applicable tenancy process before committing.
Test real routines and review the full first-month cash requirement.

sections.heading: Before arrival: establish what is already fixed
sections.body:
Put confirmed dates on one page: arrival, work location, any employer-provided accommodation and when that accommodation ends. Keep uncertain items separate. If your office location is provisional or a family member will join later, that uncertainty belongs in the housing brief rather than being hidden behind a preferred neighbourhood.

List the documents and accounts that the landlord, accommodation operator and service providers expect. Confirm the requirements for your circumstances directly; do not assume a colleague with a different residency or employment position followed the same process. Store sensitive copies securely and share only what is needed through a verified channel.

Agree a spending limit for the transition as well as the eventual monthly housing budget. Temporary accommodation, deposits, transport and setup purchases can arrive before a normal routine or income cycle is established. The annual rent alone is a poor guide to the cash you need on arrival.

sections.heading: Days one to fourteen: choose a useful base
sections.body:
A temporary base should make your first appointments and ordinary errands easier. Look at access to work, groceries, laundry and transport, and confirm the actual sleeping and working arrangements. A compact place with a practical location may serve this stage better than a larger property far from everything you need to do.

For Dubai holiday homes, [DET's hospitality guidance](https://www.dubaidet.gov.ae/en/licences-and-permits/hospitality-services-and-permits) says apartments and villas must be registered and approved before listing. Check the operator and accommodation arrangements through the appropriate channels. A short booking on a familiar platform is not, by itself, evidence that every local requirement has been met.

Read the extension and cancellation terms before booking. You may need more time, but the same unit may not remain available. The [temporary-accommodation guide](/journal/short-term-accommodation-relocation-uae) explains how to compare that flexibility and avoid treating a nightly price as the whole cost.

sections.heading: Days fifteen to thirty: turn preferences into a shortlist
sections.body:
Choose a small set of areas to investigate rather than spending every evening opening unrelated listings. Start with the journeys you expect to make most often. Visit at the times you would actually leave for work, return home or take children to school; a quiet weekend drive may give a misleading impression of the routine.

Keep notes about the building entrance, parking, walking routes and practical services. Distinguish a shop that is open from one advertised for a future phase. Notice how the route feels with bags or a pushchair, not just how short it looks on a map.

After several visits, revise the brief. You may discover that a separate working space matters more than a particular view, or that a smaller search area reduces the daily travel burden. This is useful progress, not indecision. The point of the temporary stage is to replace assumptions with experience.

sections.heading: Before signing: identify the correct tenancy process
sections.body:
The [UAE government's leasing overview](https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/moving-to-the-uae/leasing-a-property-in-the-uae) explains that registration arrangements differ by location, including Ejari in Dubai and municipal systems elsewhere. Confirm the competent authority for the exact address, particularly where a special jurisdiction applies. Avoid turning a Dubai checklist into a nationwide rule.

Review the named parties, property, term, payment schedule, deposit, inclusions and maintenance responsibilities. Ask for clarification of any early-exit or renewal terms you do not understand. Promises made while viewing should appear in the appropriate written agreement if you are relying on them.

Check that the person requesting money is authorised and that the payment instructions match the verified process. A deadline described as urgent should not prevent basic checks. Keep copies of the agreement and receipts, then confirm the registration and service-setup steps that follow rather than assuming the keys complete the administration.

rows: Whether the base supports daily needs
table.note: Original planning sequence, not a visa timetable, statutory deadline or promise that a home will be secured within ninety days.

sections.heading: Days thirty to sixty: make the home ready to occupy
sections.body:
Once a suitable home and agreement are in place, coordinate access, services and deliveries. Check building move-in arrangements before booking a van. Confirm which appliances and furniture will actually remain, and whether the home needs cleaning or agreed repairs before your belongings arrive.

The [utilities and internet guide](/journal/utilities-internet-uae-move-in) separates electricity, water, cooling and connectivity so one completed request is not mistaken for a fully ready home. Keep provider references and appointments in the same calendar as the physical move.

Buy the essentials first. A bed, basic cooking equipment and workable storage may matter more during the first week than a complete decorative scheme. Measuring the rooms and access route before ordering large items can prevent an expensive delivery problem.

sections.heading: Days sixty to ninety: review the routine you have created
sections.body:
Once the move has settled, compare the first bills and journeys with your assumptions. Check whether the payment dates fit your income cycle and whether a service charge or subscription needs clarification. Raise discrepancies while the records and conversations are easy to retrieve.

Finish the practical handover issues: missing access cards, an appliance fault, an outstanding repair or a document still awaiting confirmation. Keep a dated record of the request and response. A long-term home feels more manageable when these small unresolved items are dealt with rather than repeatedly worked around.

Finally, give the new routine time before making another major housing decision. The first weeks can be unusually busy and expensive. A considered review asks which difficulties were temporary and which belong to the location or layout itself. That distinction helps you improve the home you chose and make a clearer decision when the next housing milestone arrives.
